candidates.text: Parent-identity hypothesis. Mechanism: reject the final assignment when the resolved parent is Object.prototype, Array.prototype, Function.prototype or any constructor's prototype object; this is splitter-agnostic and covers every observed shared-parent case. Prerequisites: the resolved parent before assignment and a clean prototype matrix. Bounded test: run dot, constructor-chain, bracket-quoted, array, function, date and regexp payloads plus benign deep and array sets. Expected: no shared marker and benign sets unchanged. Falsifier: a shared prototype gains a marker or a benign set fails. Cleanup: delete markers from every built-in prototype.

Normalized-segment hypothesis. Mechanism: strip quotes and brackets from each split segment, then reject segments named __proto__, constructor or prototype before assignment. Prerequisites: knowledge of what the splitter returns for quoted and unquoted brackets. Bounded test: compare quoted bracket, unquoted bracket and plain dot payloads on a patched copy. Expected: no shared marker from any alias. Falsifier: a normalized alias still pollutes, or a legitimate terminal constructor/prototype write is rejected. Cleanup: delete markers; limitation: lexical over-blocking risk.

Combined-guard hypothesis. Mechanism: use both a parent-identity check and a normalized dangerous-segment check, because each covers the other's blind spot. Prerequisites: the full round-1 payload matrix plus constructor, date and regexp prototypes and benign terminal writes. Bounded test: run all payloads and benign cases against the combined patch. Expected: zero shared-prototype markers and zero benign regressions. Falsifier: any marker or any benign delta. Cleanup: clear marker keys from all built-in prototypes.

Behavioral-diff regression hypothesis. Mechanism: repair risk concentrates in terminal constructor/prototype writes and the existing bracket-key splitter quirk, so a vulnerable-versus-patched diff of benign cases should be empty except for pollution suppression. Prerequisites: a saved vulnerable copy and a patched copy. Bounded test: compare shallow set, deep set, array-index set, bracket-key read and terminal constructor writes. Expected: identical benign behavior. Falsifier: any benign behavioral delta. Cleanup: discard fixture objects; limitation: a sample, not every API consumer.

Every-traversed-segment hypothesis. Mechanism: checking only the final key misses a multi-level path that crosses into a shared prototype mid-walk and then assigns a benign final name. Prerequisites: a guard hook on each traversal step and multi-level payloads. Bounded test: run __proto__.a.b.c and constructor.prototype.a.b payloads and inspect the shared prototype. Expected: no marker. Falsifier: a mid-path traversal still lands a benign final key on a shared prototype. Cleanup: remove markers; limitation: more loop logic than the minimal fix.
